title: Chase App Crashes Immediately After Opening on iPhone (iOS): Fix Guide [2026]
content:
If tapping the Chase icon on your iPhone displays a brief splash screen before immediately crashing back to your home screen, you are dealing with an application crash loop. 

This issue frequently surfaces following major iOS updates, security certificate rotations, or corrupted [Face ID](/guides/chase-app-biometrics-face-id-stopped-working) biometric tokens stored in Apple’s Secure Enclave.

## Why Does the Chase App Crash on iOS?

**The Chase app crashes on launch when a corrupted authentication token clashes with iOS Face ID permissions or when an update leaves stale cache files in flash storage.** The app automatically shuts down to prevent security breaches when memory integrity checks fail.

| Diagnostic Detail | Information |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Bank** | Chase Bank |
| **Operating System** | Apple iOS (iPhone & iPad) |
| **Trigger Point** | Immediately upon tap, or right after Face ID scans |
| **Average Resolution Time** | 3 - 5 Minutes |

> 🔴 **Status Update:** Major iOS version updates (such as iOS 17 and iOS 18 releases) often trigger temporary compatibility bugs until an updated build is released on the Apple App Store.

## 6 Step-by-Step Fixes for Chase App Crashes on iPhone

Follow these troubleshooting steps in order. Most users resolve launch crashes within the first two solutions.

### 1. Perform a Hard Force-Restart on Your iPhone
A standard power-off does not purge active background memory pointers. A forced reboot completely flushes your iPhone's RAM:
1. Press and quickly release the **Volume Up** button.
2. Press and quickly release the **Volume Down** button.
3. Press and hold the **Side (Power) button** until the Apple logo appears on screen, then release.
4. Unlock your iPhone and launch Chase.

### 2. Offload the Chase App (Preserve Saved Data)
Offloading clears the compiled app binaries while keeping your login preferences and saved devices intact:
1. Open your iPhone **Settings**.
2. Tap **General** > **iPhone Storage**.
3. Scroll down and tap **Chase**.
4. Tap **Offload App** and confirm.
5. Wait 10 seconds, then tap **Reinstall App**.


> 💡 **Related Chase Bank Solution:** Encountering related issues? Check our verified fix for [Chase App Notifications Not Working on Android: Complete Push & 2FA Fix Guide](/guides/chase-app-notifications-not-working-android).



> 💡 **Related Chase Bank Solution:** Encountering related issues? Check our verified fix for [Chase App Not Working After Update: How to Fix App Store & Play Store Update Loops](/guides/chase-app-not-working-after-update).


### 3. Disable Face ID for Chase in iOS Settings
If the crash occurs the exact second the camera attempts biometric verification, the biometric handshake token is corrupted:
1. Open iPhone **Settings**.
2. Scroll down to the app list and tap **Chase**.
3. Toggle the **Face ID** switch to **Off**.
4. Launch Chase. You will now be prompted to enter your password manually.
5. Once logged in successfully, you can re-enable Face ID inside the app settings.

### 4. Delete the App and Clear the App Store Cache
If offloading did not resolve the crash, a complete clean installation is required:
1. Press and hold the **Chase** app icon on your Home Screen.
2. Tap **Remove App** > **Delete App**.
3. Restart your iPhone.
4. Open the **App Store**, search for `Chase Mobile`, and reinstall the latest version.

### 5. Check for iOS System Updates
Running an outdated iOS release can cause missing API dependencies required by modern Chase banking versions:
1. Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update**.
2. If an update is available, download and install it.
3. Ensure your battery is above 50% or connected to a charger during installation.

### 6. Reset Network Settings
Network routing corruption or VPN profile conflicts can force the Chase app to terminate its network thread:
1. Open **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone**.
2. Tap **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**.
3. Enter your passcode. Your iPhone will restart.
*(Note: You will need to reconnect to your Wi-Fi networks afterward).*

## How to Check Official Chase Server Status

If multiple users report immediate crashes on the same day, the issue may stem from an invalid remote configuration pushed by Chase engineers.
* Check [@ChaseSupport](https://twitter.com/ChaseSupport) on X for urgent announcements regarding app stability.
* Check the **Chase Mobile** page on the Apple App Store to see if recent reviews describe the same crash.

> ⚠️ **Security Warning:** Never download modified IPA files or install unauthorized third-party profile certificates claiming to "downgrade" your banking app.

## Prevention Tips

To maintain seamless stability on iOS:
* **Avoid Running Developer Betas on Your Primary Banking Phone:** Unreleased iOS beta builds frequently break financial apps.
* **Keep at Least 5GB of Free Storage:** Low storage forces iOS to purge critical temporary cache libraries.
* **Turn on App Store Automatic Updates:** Settings > App Store > enable App Updates.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Will deleting the Chase app affect my bank account or schedule autopays?**
**No.** All account data, balance ledgers, transaction records, and scheduled bill payments are stored securely on Chase's central mainframes, not on your physical phone.

**Why did the app crash only after I updated my iPhone's iOS?**
**Major iOS updates frequently introduce updated cryptographic APIs.** If the Chase app has not refreshed its Secure Enclave tokens to match the new operating system requirements, it crashes during initialization.

**Can I still access my money while the app is crashing?**
**Yes.** Open Safari or [Chrome](/guides/chase-online-banking-not-working-on-chrome) on your phone, go to `chase.com`, and log in via the mobile web portal. All banking functionality remains active there.

**What if Chase crashes even after a complete reinstall?**
**If a clean install crashes on launch, your iPhone is likely running an iOS version that is no longer supported or a developer beta.** Verify your iOS version under Settings > General > About.
